basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 1.' and it opens '(Cap. XXXIII.—Vers. 1 et 2.) Et divisit pueros super Liam et super Rachel, et super duas'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XXXIII.—Vers. 1 et 2.) Et divisit pueros super Liam et super Rachel, et super duas ancillas, et posuit ancillas et filios earum primos: Liam vero et pueros ejus novissimos, et Rachel et Joseph novissimos, et ipse transivit ante eos. Non, ut plerique aestimant, tres turmas fecit, sed duas. Denique ubi nos habemus, divisit, Aquila posuit, ἡμίσευσεν, id est, dimidiavit: ut unum cuneum faceret ancillarum cum parvulis suis, et alium Liae, et Rachel, quae liberae erant, cum filiis earum: primasque ire faceret ancillas, secundas liberas: ipse autem ante utrumque gregem, fratrem adoraturus occurreret.
